2608.27345.title: PAWBench: How Far Are We from Probabilistically Aligned World Modeling?
2608.27345.paper_summary: Recent video generation models are increasingly framed as world models. Many physical processes can unfold in more than one valid way. Therefore, a world model should reproduce not only a plausible trajectory, but also the distribution of possible behaviors under the same initial observation and action. We call this distribution-level requirement probabilistic alignment. However, existing evaluations largely assess individual-video plausibility and do not test whether repeated generations recover the correct distribution. This raises a central question: how far are current video generators from probabilistically aligned world modeling? To answer it, we formalize probabilistic alignment as a distributional criterion for world models and introduce PAWBench, a benchmark for evaluating video generators as stochastic samplers of world dynamics. We further introduce PAWEval, an outcome-level protocol that converts repeated video rollouts into empirical distributions over possible physical behaviors. Across 50 scenarios and eleven current systems, no model consistently matches the reference probabilities while recovering the range of valid behaviors. Having established this gap, we test whether language prompts, initial noise sampling, or model training can reshape the model's predictive distribution. We believe our work can serve as a foundation for future efforts to move towards probabilistically aligned world modeling.
2608.27345.paper_summary_zh: 最近的視頻生成模型越來越多地被框架化為世界模型。許多物理過程可以以多種有效的方式展開。因此，世界模型應該不僅重現一條合理的軌跡，還應該重現在相同初始觀察和行動下可能行為的分佈。我們稱這一分佈層級的要求為概率對齊。然而，現有的評估主要評估單個視頻的合理性，而不測試重複生成是否恢復了正確的分佈。這提出了一個核心問題：當前的視頻生成器距離概率對齊的世界建模有多遠？為了解答這個問題，我們將概率對齊形式化為世界模型的分佈標準，並引入PAWBench，一個用於評估視頻生成器作為世界動態隨機採樣器的基準。我們進一步引入PAWEval，一個結果層級的協議，將重複的視頻展開轉換為可能物理行為的實證分佈。在50個場景和11個當前系統中，沒有模型能夠一致地匹配參考概率，同時恢復有效行為的範圍。在確立了這一差距後，我們測試了語言提示、初始噪聲採樣或模型訓練是否能重塑模型的預測分佈。我們相信我們的工作可以作為未來努力朝著概率對齊的世界建模邁進的基礎。
